cards.text: Isaiah, the prophet, has just been talking about a king who will reign in righteousness (Isaiah 32:1). Now he opens with a woe aimed at someone who's been wrecking everything and never paying for it. He calls him, "O destroyer never destroyed, O traitor never betrayed!"

cards.question: This destroyer has torn everything up and never been torn up back. What does Isaiah say happens when he's finished destroying?
Isaiah says the traitor who betrayed everyone will never be betrayed himself.

cards.text: Friend, that destroyer is the coworker who's been sneaking the last cookie out of the break room box for YEARS. Then one day he opens the box, and somebody beat HIM to it.
Then the voice turns to the LORD in prayer: "O LORD, be gracious to us! We wait for You."

cards.question: In this prayer, the people ask the LORD to be their strength only in time of trouble.

cards.text: Then the prayer turns to the LORD's power. His voice is like thunder, and He rises up.

cards.question: When the LORD rises and His voice thunders, what do the nations do?
Isaiah tells the nations about their spoil. He says men sweep over it like a swarm of ___.

cards.text: Then Isaiah looks up. The LORD is exalted, because He lives on high, and He has filled His city, Zion.

cards.question: What has the LORD filled Zion with?

cards.text: The LORD will be the sure foundation for your times, a storehouse of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer stuffed with takeout menus and warranty cards, and not ONE of them ever saved anybody.

cards.question: With the LORD as that kind of storehouse, what does Isaiah call Zion's treasure?

cards.text: Then the picture flips back to right now: their valiant ones cry aloud in the streets. The tough guys are crying, friend, the TOUGH guys.

cards.question: The envoys sent out to make peace are in the streets too. How are they doing?

cards.text: The highways are deserted, and travel has ceased. Rush hour with nobody honking, nobody merging, NOBODY on the road.

cards.question: With the roads empty, Isaiah says at least the treaty still holds and the witnesses are honored.

cards.text: Even the land mourns and languishes. Lebanon is ashamed and decayed, and Bashan and Carmel shake off their leaves.

cards.question: The land is mourning. Isaiah says Sharon is like a ___.

cards.text: Things are about as low as they can get. Then the LORD Himself speaks, and He says He will arise, lift Himself up and be exalted.

cards.question: With the land at its lowest, when does the LORD say He will arise and be exalted?

cards.text: Then He says, "You conceive chaff; you give birth to stubble." Friend, that's me mixing and stamping a giant batch for an HOUR, opening the oven, and finding nothing but crumbs.

cards.question: The LORD tells the ones who conceive chaff that their own breath is a fire that will ___ them.
The LORD says the peoples will be burned to ashes, like thorns cut down and set ablaze.

cards.text: Then the LORD calls out for people to hear what He has done and acknowledge His might.

cards.question: The LORD's call to hear what He has done is only for those who are near.

cards.text: The sinners in Zion are afraid, and trembling grips the ungodly. I bet they're shaking like somebody who just heard the boss say, "Got a minute?"

cards.question: Trembling, the ungodly in Zion ask a question. What do they ask?

answers.text: Who can dwell with a consuming fire
When the enemy will finally leave
Where the nearest city of refuge is

cards.text: And an answer comes. It's the one who walks righteously and speaks with sincerity.

cards.question: The person described here refuses gain from extortion, and his hand never takes a bribe.
This person stops his ___ against murderous plots and shuts his ___ tightly against evil.

cards.text: And that person gets to live on the heights. Friend, my last address was the back of a junk drawer under a takeout menu, and this guy gets the HEIGHTS.

cards.question: This person will live on the heights. What does Isaiah say will be his refuge there?
The person who walks righteously will still have to worry about his food and water.

cards.text: Now the message turns, and it gets bright. Isaiah tells the listener what their own eyes will see.

cards.question: Isaiah says their eyes will see someone. Who?
Along with the King, their eyes will behold a land that stretches afar.

cards.text: They'll think back on the old terror and ask, "Where is he who tallies? Where is he who weighs? Where is he who counts the towers?" That's the guy who counted every cookie in the box so nobody could sneak one, and one day he's just GONE.

cards.question: Isaiah says they will still have to deal with the insolent people whose language they can't understand.

cards.text: Then Isaiah says to look upon Zion, the city of their appointed feasts. Jerusalem will be a peaceful pasture, and a tent.

cards.question: Its tent pegs won't be pulled up, and none of its cords will break. Jerusalem will be a tent that does not ___.

cards.text: And there, the Majestic One, our LORD, will be for them a place of rivers and wide canals.

cards.question: Galleys with oars and majestic vessels will row and sail on those rivers.

cards.text: Then Isaiah says why they can rest easy: "For the LORD is our Judge, the LORD is our lawgiver, the LORD is our King."

cards.question: The LORD is their Judge, their lawgiver and their King. What does Isaiah say He will do for them?

cards.text: "Your ropes are slack; they cannot secure the mast or spread the sail." A ship that can't do the one thing it's built for is a cookie stamper with blurry stamps, and friend, I KNOW that feeling.

cards.question: Then an abundance of spoils gets divided. Who carries off plunder?

cards.text: And the message ends with the people who live in Zion. Not one of them will say they're sick.

cards.question: What happens to the iniquity of the people who dwell in Zion?

findings.problem: The card says the destroyer has been "wrecking everything." Isaiah 33:1 calls him a destroyer and a traitor but never says he destroyed everything. Papa Dorin is stating this as a Bible fact, not making a joke.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The question says the destroyer "has torn everything up." Isaiah 33:1 never says "everything."

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The statement calls him "the traitor who betrayed everyone." Isaiah 33:1 says only "O traitor never betrayed" and never says he betrayed everyone.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke about verse 1, which cards 1 to 3 already covered. It tells no new part of the passage and doesn't move the baker forward. The joke should ride along on a card that carries the passage.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: "Things are about as low as they can get" is stated as fact, and card 2 builds on it with "With the land at its lowest." Isaiah 33:7-9 describe mourning and ruin, but the text never says things are at their lowest point.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: This is a "Who?" question. "An army at the gates" is a generic group, not a real Bible detail, and it isn't the same kind of answer as the two single persons (the King, Elijah).

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: Card 8 tells only that the LORD will be "a place of rivers and wide canals." That points a thoughtful baker toward True, because rivers and canals suggest ships, but the answer is False. Nothing in the setup lets the baker reason out that no ship will pass. Card 8 should give enough context, or the card should ask something else.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The card uses a fact from Isaiah 32:1, which is outside the passage, and cites it in the text as (Isaiah 32:1). The card's verses field says only Isaiah 33:1.
findings.question: When a story card uses a fact from outside the passage with an inline reference, should the card's verses field include that outside verse, or only the passage verses it tells? Should an inline reference appear in card text at all?
